literaryJudgment.sustainedStory: The pursuit at the inn, Silver’s charm and conspiracy, the two accounts of the island, Jim’s unauthorised sea excursion, reciprocal bargains, hunt, disclosure and aftermath unfold as actual scenes. Fear, humour, changes of trust and the nightmare ending remain in the telling.
literaryJudgment.narratorBoundary: Jim narrates what he experiences and learns later. Livesey explicitly takes overXVI–XVIII; Jim resumesXIX. The treasure transfer and rescue chronology are disclosed by the doctor only after the pit scene.
literaryJudgment.authorDifficulties: Jim admits his unauthorised departures and exaggerated captive boast. Silver’s kindness, threats, self-preservation, later temptation and escape remain connected; the digest does not settle him into a single moral lesson. Livesey’s urge to save Jim conflicts with the parole promise in the actual scene.
literaryJudgment.ending: Ben’s past work, three abandoned men and their supplies, escape, five returning original voyagers and distinct later lives are retained. Silver’s later life remains unknown; Jim’s final nightmare remains the narrative ending.
literaryJudgment.shorterRoutes: Both stop after the stockade battle and honestly disclose their unresolved opening scope. Essential now includes the actual council before shore departure; Core retains the complete opening throughXXI. Neither exposes the later sea/hunt/return outcomes.
literaryJudgment.depthDecision: 93 sustained narrative paragraphs cover all34chapters, with concrete action, relationships and changing knowledge. The word/screen counts describe that telling; they are neither a universal minimum nor the reason for acceptance.
